answer_summary: Energy released per 235U fission event: ΔE = 233 × 8.45 − 235 × 7.59 = 1968.85 − 1783.65 = 185.2 MeV, reported as 185 MeV (three significant figures). The reaction is the 4.3 fission equation 235U + n → 93Rb + 140Cs + 3n (Rb and Cs are both group-1 elements; 93+140+3 = 236, 37+55 = 92), derived from the printed shared context (three emitted neutrons), the printed yield-curve peaks at A ≈ 93 and A ≈ 140, mass/charge conservation, and the same-group condition.
assumptions: 'this reaction' in 4.4 refers to the 4.3 fission equation 235U + n → 93Rb + 140Cs + 3n, derived inline from problem-only inputs (three emitted neutrons per the shared context, yield-curve peaks at A ≈ 93 and 140, same-group condition, mass and charge conservation). The numeric result depends only on the conserved nucleon counts (235 bound initially, 233 bound finally), not on the specific fragment identities.

The absorbed neutron and the three emitted neutrons all carry zero binding energy, per the printed instruction to neglect the binding energy of free neutrons and the fact that the absorbed neutron is free.

The printed binding energies BE(235U) = 7.59 MeV/nucleon and BE(fis.) = 8.45 MeV/nucleon are treated as exact stipulated constants, per the measurement policy for stipulated constants; no tolerance intervals are propagated.
Final display uses the project-wide answer-blind default of three significant figures (185 MeV at quantum 1 MeV); the raw value 185.2 MeV is exact and no intermediate rounding is performed.
